abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy has transformed RNA structural biology, revealing increasingly large and complex structures at an unprecedented pace. However, validation methods have lagged behind, and deposited models can contain distorted base pairs, incorrect ribose puckers and backbone conformational outliers. Here, we introduce Rapid Unified Base-pair, Ribose and backbone Integrity Check (RUBRIC), an open-source program that combines RNA structural annotation with local validation of base pairs, sugars, and backbones. RUBRIC assigns Leontis-Westhof classes and identifies geometrically ambiguous pairs that cannot be confidently assigned to a single class. It scores unambiguous pairs against reference geometries for each type and class, identifying the parameters responsible for low scores. It also assigns backbone suites to known conformers, suggests target torsions for unassigned suites and flags incorrect ribose puckers. RUBRIC analyzes a complete human ribosome in under a second, with base-pair detection and classification consistent with leading annotation programs. These programs disagreed significantly more often on pairs RUBRIC flagged as ambiguous than on unambiguous pairs. The geometric problems flagged by RUBRIC were reduced in higher-resolution models of the same RNA or after refinement targeting the affected geometry, indicating that these problems are correctable. A PyMOL plug-in and machine-readable output support model building, correction before deposition and assessment of deposited structures before reuse. RUBRIC can therefore help improve RNA structures in the PDB and the datasets used to train and evaluate RNA structure prediction methods.
